annotator_prompt.name: bin_center
annotator_prompt.description: After a cube was lifted, the bin opening could be obscured in both current views although it had been visible earlier. The policy chose a visibility-recovery lift instead of the recorded closed transfer. Counts and held_color did not preserve the missing spatial fact, breaking SUFFICIENCY. Add bin_center, holding the reliably reconstructed world xy center of the stationary bin's inner opening, or unknown before a reliable reconstruction is available. Set it at the first cycle whose available calibrated views constrain that center; retain it through occlusion and subsequent transfers, releases, and retreats. Revise it only when newly reliable geometry establishes a corrected center or an observed displacement of the bin. Do not fill earlier cycles using geometry available only later in the episode, and do not copy the recorded transfer waypoint as a substitute for visual reconstruction. Example value: [-0.0175, -0.089].

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: bin_center
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: A lifted cube or the hand can obscure an opening that was previously localizable. Without its retained center, the policy unnecessarily takes a recovery lift, breaking SUFFICIENCY. Initialize bin_center to unknown. When this cycle's calibrated views reliably constrain the inner opening using the action instruction's geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks, write its world xy center, for example [-0.0175, -0.089]. Otherwise retain the incoming value. In particular, do not overwrite a reliable center with an estimate based only on a cropped dark region, an occluding silhouette, or measured TCP position. Update an established value only when reliable current geometry supports a correction or shows that the bin moved. If movement is visibly established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. The field records observed bin geometry, never the destination of an action merely being selected.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: When a held cube had reached lift height, requiring fresh bin localization sometimes produced an unnecessary recovery lift; other transfers used inaccurate estimates from partial rim views. The former is a SUFFICIENCY failure because earlier observable geometry was lost. Replace the unconditional requirement to re-estimate the bin center each cycle with this rule: use a reliable current reconstruction when available; otherwise use incoming bin_center unless current observations establish that the bin moved. Use that same center for closed transfer at z=0.20, the separate centered opening operation, and retreat at [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20]. A partial or cropped current view does not invalidate a retained center. Perform visibility recovery only when neither current geometry nor retained memory supplies a reliable center. Keep the existing inner-rim reconstruction and reprojection checks; do not replace them with episode-specific coordinates. At release, correct both lateral coordinates to the opening center before checking the nonzero-motion requirement; a sufficient lateral correction makes an added vertical displacement unnecessary. All deposit-count, held-color, grasp, final-retreat, and button-contact rules remain unchanged.
proposal.refused: The reports of ambiguous cube selection correctly identify a SUFFICIENCY gap: eligibility and clear-grasp preferences do not uniquely predict which accessible cube the recording selects. However, their proposed scene-specific choices do not establish a common executable ranking. Nearest-to-hand, robot-rightmost, and isolated-foreground preferences are not interchangeable, and imposing any one globally would contradict other recorded selections. One report also describes the next selected object as a foreground green cube while assigning it the coordinates of a distant blue cube; the subsequent grasp and blue deposit confirm that the selected cube was blue. Do not add that color claim, a per-scene choice table, a prescribed color order, or a future-target memory field. The target-selection gap remains unresolved by this minibatch; resolving it requires an independently supported selection criterion, not pretending that arbitrary recorded choices are recoverable historical facts. Reports of inaccurate bin reconstruction are addressed only by retaining genuinely observed geometry where it later becomes unavailable. Their numerical targets are not general rules and must not be hard-coded. Reports that release should correct the measured TCP to the opening center repeat an existing rule, retained explicitly above rather than introducing another stage or memory flag. The incorrect descent onto a neighboring cube and the small cube/button localization errors likewise do not demonstrate missing history: current calibrated views provide the relevant centers, and existing instructions already require maintaining the aligned cube, using its top face, and localizing the circular button top. No new memory is justified for those errors, and no deposit-count or held_color annotation change is supported.

fields.name: deposited_blue
fields.description: Include only when blue is requested. Initialize to 0 when memory is empty; otherwise carry forward. Increment once when this cycle's incoming motion shows either a blue cube carried over the bin followed by an empty open hand, or a blue cube separating or falling directly below the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand. The sampled frames need not show the finger-opening transition itself. Require evidence of a new release from this hand over the bin; a stationary tabletop cube below the hand or an unrelated falling cube is not release evidence. Identify color from the carried or newly released cube, not remaining tabletop objects. Alternatively, when incoming held_color is blue, count a newly established transition to an empty open hand over the bin in the executed incoming release motion, with no evidence of loss elsewhere, even if all sampled frames omit the cube. Use incoming held_color before clearing it. This is an alternative evidence test for the same release, not an additional increment; an already empty hand or a no-step motion does not qualify. Count even if the resting cube is hidden and even if the motion includes retreat. Never increment for the command about to be issued, an already empty hand, a grasp, a closed transfer, retreat without a new release, or a motion executing no steps. Preserve through button pressing. e.g. 2

Do not increment when merely choosing the opening command, for grasps or closed transfers, or for later views of a completed release. Preserve otherwise, including through button pressing. e.g. 2

Never increment for the command about to be issued, an already empty hand, a grasp, a closed transfer, retreat without a new release, or a motion executing no steps. Preserve through button pressing. e.g. 3
fields.annotation: Include only when red is requested. Cumulative number of red cubes released from the gripper into the bin during execution, initially 0. Increment once at the first act cycle whose incoming motion contains the completed red release over the opening, including release followed by retreat. Identify color before release; count even when the deposited cube becomes hidden. Do not increment when merely choosing the opening command, for grasps or closed transfers, or for later views of a completed release. Preserve otherwise, including through button pressing. e.g. 3

fields.name: held_color
fields.description: Values are none, blue, green, or red. Initialize to none. Set to the visibly grasped cube's color when current views and finger opening establish a successful grasp. Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary visual occlusion while possession remains supported. When the hand becomes empty, evaluate deposit updates using incoming held_color before writing none. Clear without counting when loss occurs away from the bin. Do not set from a future grasp target or clear merely because an opening command is about to be issued. e.g. red
fields.annotation: Color of the cube currently held: none, blue, green, or red. Initially none. Set to the cube's color at the first cycle showing a successful grasp. Retain through closed lifting and transfer, including temporary occlusion while possession remains supported. Clear to none at the first cycle showing the hand empty after release or loss. Record observed possession, not a selected grasp target or an opening command about to execute. Deposit-count annotations retain their existing completed-release timing. e.g. red

fields.name: bin_center
fields.description: World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initialize to unknown. When this cycle's calibrated views reliably constrain the center using the action instruction's geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks, write that center. Otherwise retain the incoming value through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Update an established value only when reliable current geometry supports a correction or establishes bin displacement. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. A cropped view or partial occlusion alone does not invalidate the retained center. Do not overwrite it with the centroid of a visible dark fragment, an occluding silhouette, measured TCP position, or the destination of an action being selected. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]
fields.annotation: World xy center of the bin's inner opening, written as [x, y] in metres, or unknown. Initially unknown. Set at the first cycle whose available calibrated views reliably constrain the center using geometric reconstruction and reprojection checks. Retain through occlusion, transfers, releases, and retreats. Revise only when reliable current geometry establishes a correction or an observed displacement of the bin. If displacement is established but the new center cannot be reconstructed, write unknown. Use only geometry available by this cycle; do not backfill from later views or substitute recorded action destinations for visual reconstruction. e.g. [-0.02, -0.09]

texts.action:
Read a separate quota for each requested color from the goal each cycle. For each color, compute its completed count from its incoming deposited_<color> memory plus only that color's newly completed release in the current incoming motion, exactly once, using the memory instruction's sparse-frame evidence test. A carried cube followed by an empty open hand, or a cube visibly separating or falling from the fingers over the opening followed by an empty open hand, can establish the release without a sampled finger-opening transition. Also apply the memory instruction's incoming-held_color test when the released cube is absent from all incoming samples. Evaluate that test before clearing held_color, and compute completion from the resulting per-color counts, not from outgoing held_color. Multiple evidence tests for one release still produce only one increment. Do not add the release again to an already updated count. A color is eligible only while its own quota remains outstanding. Completion requires every requested color's quota to be satisfied. Start with an open hand and zero deposits for each requested color. Infer object positions from calibrated front and wrist views rather than treating image coordinates as world coordinates. Cubes are approximately 4 cm wide: identify and back-project their top-face centers at approximately z=0.04 and use the resulting world xy for approach and the z=0.02 grasp. Use the top face, not the whole visible silhouette; visible side faces must not bias the center. For the bin center, use a reliable current reconstruction when available; otherwise use incoming bin_center unless current observations establish that the bin moved. Partial occlusion or cropping alone does not invalidate a retained center. To obtain or reliably correct the center, reconstruct the bin's rectangular inner opening using the available calibrated current views. For each image point [u,v,1], form a world ray with camera center C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], using that camera's current calibration. Prefer reliable two-view correspondences between actual inner-rim corners or edge intersections: triangulate them and fit their common horizontal plane. When such correspondences are unavailable, accept a single-view reconstruction if visible geometry constrains it. Identify actual table-contact base corners and their corresponding vertical wall edges; intersect base-corner rays with z=0, then fit corresponding upper corners along the world-vertical lines through those base corners to determine the rim plane. Back-project inner-rim edge points into that plane and fit the rectangular opening. Use visible opposing edges and reconstruct obscured portions only where the fitted geometry constrains them. Compute the world center from opposing corners or edge midlines, and verify reprojection against all available visible rim segments, including partial wrist edges. Do not shift the center toward a visible side wall, use the centroid of an exposed dark fragment, average image centroids across cameras, treat occluding silhouettes as rim correspondences, or intersect the opening center with the tabletop. A cropped wrist view or partial opening occlusion alone does not require visibility recovery. Use the purposeful visibility-recovery motion below only when neither current geometry nor a valid retained bin_center supplies a reliable center; do not invent a numeric rim height. Use the center selected by this current-reconstruction-or-memory rule consistently for closed transfer and separate release at z=0.20 and for retreat at [bin_x-0.10,bin_y,0.20]. Locate the button by its gray circular top on a light square base; back-project the top center at approximately z=0.02 and use that xy for approach and press. Re-estimate cube and button positions from current views; scene objects can appear during execution. For the bin, apply the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule rather than requiring fresh localization. Robot right is negative world y.

When any color quota remains outstanding and the hand is empty away from the bin's release position, select a visible, accessible tabletop cube of an eligible color. Prefer a clear grasp and maintain the selection when the hand is already aligned above an eligible cube; do not switch cubes or colors simply because new cubes appear. Never select another cube of a color whose quota is already satisfied. Approach its center at z=0.15 with the gripper open, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, and a feasible yaw aligned with a cube edge. Do not constrain yaw to [-0.7854,0.7854]. Re-estimate edge alignment for each newly selected cube rather than carrying over the previous cube's yaw, and preserve the selected orientation through descent and lift. When already above an eligible cube near z=0.15, identify the approached cube by projecting [current_tcp_x,current_tcp_y,0.04] into the current wrist image with its calibration. Identify the eligible top face nearest that projection, cross-checking world-space proximity and the incoming approach frames. Neither the wrist image center nor the largest visible cube is the alignment reference. Refine that same cube's top-face center at approximately z=0.04, then descend at its world xy to z=0.02 and close, preserving the approached cube's edge-aligned orientation. Do not switch to another prominent cube or descend at an inaccurate measured approach xy.

When a cube is grasped at table height, lift vertically to z=0.15, retaining its grasp orientation and keeping the gripper closed. A cube between the fingers and finger positions around 0.018 m support a successful grasp. Once lifted, move to the world xy center of the bin opening supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule at z=0.20, keeping the cube closed in the gripper and preserving the measured grasp orientation. After the closed-hand transfer reaches approximately z=0.20 above the bin, use that same rule to obtain the opening center and command open at [bin_x, bin_y, 0.20], correcting any residual lateral error in that waypoint. The target is the opening center, not the measured TCP xy. Opening remains a separate operation from the closed-hand transfer. Correct both lateral coordinates before testing whether the centered target would produce no motion; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only in that case.

When the hand is empty and open at the bin after a release, including a release established using incoming held_color without a sampled separation, retreat toward the robot: target [bin_x-0.10, bin_y, 0.20], preserving orientation and keeping open. Compute this offset from the bin center supplied by the current-reconstruction-or-memory rule, never from measured TCP xy. Perform this retreat even after the final requested cube. If the incoming motion already included this retreat and the hand is at that offset, do not repeat it. Retreat clears the opening and gives the dropped cube time to fall; no separate arbitrary wait is needed.

When every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is finished, ignore all remaining cubes. Approach the button center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, with the gripper open. When already aligned above the button with open fingers, re-localize the gray circular button-top center, back-projecting it at approximately z=0.02 and checking the other current view when visible. Use the circular top, not the surrounding square base. Command [button_x,button_y,0.15,-3.1416,0,0] and close the empty gripper. Correct the target before testing the nonzero-motion requirement; add a 0.003 m vertical displacement only if the corrected target would otherwise produce no motion. When aligned above the button with closed fingers, descend to [button_x, button_y, 0.0075] with the gripper closed. If the current motion shows this descent reaching button contact, retract to [button_x, button_y, 0.15] with the gripper still closed. Contact can leave the measured TCP near z=0.0245 rather than the commanded depth; recognize the visible contact and retract instead of repeatedly demanding a deeper press.

For an unanticipated or ambiguous situation, use the visible hand contents, finger opening, height, and object alignment to recover the applicable rule. Never increase the deposit count without an observed release. If a grasp fails, reopen with a small nonzero upward motion and re-approach a visible requested-color cube. If any color quota remains outstanding but no suitable cube of an eligible color is currently available, wait 16 control steps specifically to observe newly arriving cubes, then reassess. If occlusion leaves an object needed for localization genuinely underconstrained after using the available calibrated views and visible geometry, and for the bin no valid retained bin_center supplies its center, move upward to a clear viewing height while retaining any held cube, then re-localize. Do not make this recovery motion merely because the wrist view crops the object or part of it is hidden. Never press the stop button before every requested color's quota is satisfied and the final release retreat is complete.

applied.refused: The earlier rejection of remembered bin coordinates is superseded only because this round establishes that previously observable bin geometry can become unavailable in both current views. The new field preserves that observed fact; it does not replace calibrated reconstruction or authorize copying recorded waypoints. No scene-specific coordinates, fixed rim height, target-choice table, color priority, nearest-cube rule, or future-target memory is added. Across rounds these selection proposals remain inconsistent and do not establish a predictable general ranking. No duplicate release-correction stage, yaw history, cube/button position memory, or changes to deposit counts and held_color are committed: the existing rules cover those operations, and this round establishes no additional missing historical fact.
